questions.q: Why does this DAO's treasury sit behind a TimelockController instead of letting the Governor execute a passed proposal immediately?
options: A mandatory delay gives the community a window to notice and react before a malicious or mistaken proposal can move funds
TimelockController makes transactions free of gas costs
The Governor contract is incapable of holding any state
A timelock permanently prevents the treasury from ever spending money
questions.explain: The lesson states the timelock's entire purpose is the mandatory delay window between a passed vote and execution.

questions.q: In the TimelockController constructor, what does the minDelay parameter actually control?
options: The minimum number of seconds before a queued operation can execute
The minimum number of votes needed to pass a proposal
The minimum token balance required to submit a proposal
The minimum gas price for any transaction
questions.explain: The lesson defines minDelay as the real, enforced wait time in seconds, and warns that a near-zero delay provides no real protection.

questions.q: In this project's design, who is granted the PROPOSER_ROLE on the timelock?
options: The Governor contract itself, not any individual person
The original contract deployer, permanently
Every token holder equally
No one -- PROPOSER_ROLE is unused in this design
questions.explain: The lesson specifies that the Governor is granted PROPOSER_ROLE so only successful governance votes can queue operations.

questions.q: Why might a project deliberately grant EXECUTOR_ROLE to the zero address?
options: Because once the delay has passed on an already-approved call, there's no remaining reason to restrict who can trigger it
Because the zero address is the only valid Solidity address
Because it disables execution entirely
Because it grants the deployer permanent control
questions.explain: The lesson describes opening EXECUTOR_ROLE to anyone as a common, deliberate choice once a call has already cleared the delay.

questions.q: What does renouncing the deployer's TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE after setup actually accomplish?
options: It removes the deployer's ability to grant themselves proposer or executor rights and bypass governance entirely
It permanently locks the treasury so no proposal can ever execute
It transfers all treasury funds to the deployer
It has no real effect and is purely symbolic
questions.explain: The lesson calls this the step that actually makes the system decentralized -- without it, a standing admin could bypass the vote at any time.
